turns.t: Okay, you can head in now. Room two, on the left.
Hi there. Are you Marcus Delaney? Is that right?
Yeah.
Great, come on in and grab the chair. I'm Dr Ellis. What brings you in today?
A cough.
A cough. Tell me about it.
It's at night. Mostly.
At night.
It wakes me up. Every night, kind of.
Every night. How long has that been going on?
Like two weeks.
Two weeks. And is there anything that makes it worse?
Lying down. It's better when I sit up.
Sitting up helps. Okay.
My dad's parking the car. He'll be in soon.
No problem. Do you get a fever with it?
No.
Good. Have you ever had an operation, Marcus?
Tonsils. When I was six.
When you were six. Okay. Let me listen to your chest. Lift your shirt for me, and breathe in and out nice and slowly.
Is it cold?
A little, sorry. Big breath in. And out.
Your chest sounds clear all the way through. Nothing worrying in there.
Doctor, sorry, your next one called to say they're running ten minutes late.
Thanks, that gives us time. Marcus, so here's what I think.
Okay.
It sounds most likely like a post-nasal drip, where mucus drips down the back of your throat when you lie flat, and that tickles the cough.
Gross.
Pretty common, though. I don't think we need to prescribe anything. A few simple changes should help.
Like what?
Prop an extra pillow under your head. Drink some water before bed, and keep your room from getting too dry.
I can do the pillow.
Perfect. If it's still going in two weeks, come back and we'll take another look.
Okay. Two weeks. Thanks.
You're welcome, Marcus. Your dad can sit with you in the waiting room if he's in by now.
